title: De Revolutionibus Veritatis  -  Rework Deliverable (Phase 1-3)

canonical_node.axiom: The rework must align the series with the May 10 Formal Theory canon, reclassifying claims and correcting structural inconsistencies before any rewriting.
definitions: May 10 Formal Theory v1.0: The canonical reference document defining the three primitive axioms, seven forced conclusions, and typed factors.
Below-floor presupposition: Properties of Truth that are pre-system constraints, not axioms within the system.
Load-bearing: A claim whose reclassification or removal would alter the argument's structure or conclusions.
No-drift rule: The Layer-1 definition of the Master Equation factors wins over any other usage in the series.
derivation: The 20 axioms in drv-02 are not axioms under the May 10 canon; they are a mix of presuppositions, theorems, derivations, definitions, and one primitive axiom.
The Master Equation in drv-00 uses variable assignments that conflict with Definition 10 of the canon; the no-drift rule requires correction.
The series has internal numbering and scope drift (e.g., Book ordering, Tetralogy vs. Six Books, missing Book V) that must be resolved before structural rework.
The rework plan prioritizes resolving load-bearing structural issues first, then applying minor cleanups and new sections.
canonical_node.action: Approve, modify, or reject the Phase 1-3 deliverable before Phase 4 execution; if approved, execute the recommended order starting with the decision pass.
boundary: This deliverable stops at Phase 3; no rewriting has happened.
It does not resolve the five decisions; it only recommends options.
It does not provide formal proofs for the reclassifications; it relies on the May 10 canon as authority.
test: Check that all reclassifications match the May 10 canon's taxonomy.
Verify that the Master Equation variable assignments are corrected to Definition 10.
Confirm that the series numbering and scope inconsistencies are resolved per the decisions.
Ensure that the recommended execution order is followed in Phase 4.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a structured rework plan that reclassifies the series' foundational claims under the May 10 canon, corrects variable assignments, and resolves numbering/scope inconsistencies.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the May 10 Formal Theory as the authoritative canon and the Iron Chain as supporting derivation context.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this deliverable, the series would continue to use outdated axiom classifications and inconsistent variable assignments, undermining its alignment with the canon.
dg5_translation_registers: Theology: Reclassifies axioms as presuppositions, theorems, derivations, definitions, or primitive axioms.
Physics: Corrects Master Equation variable assignments to match Definition 10.
Mathematics: Identifies theorems like Gdel/Chaitin and derivations from Kolmogorov bounds.

classification.recommended_atom_action: Approve as a planning document; do not treat as a proof of the underlying claims.

overstatement_risks: The reclassifications are asserted based on the May 10 canon but not formally proven here.
The recommendation to mark Book V abandoned may be premature if the content is later needed.
The probability calculation rebuild is flagged as needing a defensible constraint set, but no new calculation is provided.
kill_conditions: If the May 10 canon is superseded or revised, the rework plan becomes obsolete.
If the decisions are not resolved, Phase 4 cannot proceed coherently.
If the Lindblad mapping is not formally reconciled, the theological mappings remain rhetorical.
risk.lean_target: The rework plan itself is not a formal proof; it is a meta-document. The underlying claims require separate formal verification.

plain_summary: This document is a Phase 1-3 deliverable that audits the series' axioms and structure against the May 10 Formal Theory canon. It identifies three key findings: the 20 axioms are misclassified, the Master Equation has wrong variable assignments, and there are numbering/scope inconsistencies. It provides a detailed rework plan with priorities, decisions required, and open questions. It does not rewrite anything yet; it awaits approval for Phase 4.
